title: An everywhere-defined graded Proj immersion detects relative ampleness
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\mathcal A_d$ be a quasi-coherent graded commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra, def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. It need not be generated in degree one and $\mathcal A_0$ need not equal $\mathcal O_S$. Suppose $\psi:h^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\ge0}L^{\otimes d}$ is a graded algebra homomorphism [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $U(\psi)$ be the union, over $d\ge1$, of the open loci on which $\psi_d:h^*\mathcal A_d\to L^{\otimes d}$ is surjective, and let $r_{L,\psi}:U(\psi)\to\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal A)$ be the canonical morphism [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map, def-nagata-relative-proj]. If $U(\psi)=Z$ and $r_{L,\psi}$ is an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], then $L|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for every affine open $V\subseteq S$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), implication (6) implies (1), with the generation locus and canonical map from Constructions Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj).

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V\subseteq S$, put $T=h^{-1}(V)$, and write $A=\mathcal A(V)$ and $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$. The affine restriction of the relative Proj and of the canonical map in [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] identifies $r_{L,\psi}|_T$ with the ordinary canonical morphism $r:T\to P$ attached to the graded ring map $A\to\Gamma_*(T,L|_T)$ induced by $\psi$. Because $U(\psi)=Z$, the positive-degree images generate $L|_T$ at every point, so the nonvanishing opens of positive-degree homogeneous sections cover $T$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, proof of (6) implies (1), affine reduction; Constructions Tag 01O9, affine restriction and canonical map.

proof.text: The morphism $r:T\to P$ is an immersion and $T$ is quasi-compact, since $h$ is quasi-compact and $V$ is affine. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-shrink-to-closed-exists] there is a quasi-compact open $Y\subseteq P$ containing $r(T)$ such that the induced morphism $i:T\to Y$ is a closed immersion; with $u:Y\to P$ the open inclusion, $r=u\circ i$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, proof of (6) implies (1), paragraph asserting that quasi-compact X is a closed subscheme of a quasi-compact open Y in Proj(A).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample], there is an integer $e\geq1$ for which $\mathcal O_Y(e)$ is invertible and ample. Restricting this ample module along the closed immersion $i$ and using [lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion] shows that $i^*\mathcal O_Y(e)$ is ample on $T$. Via $u^*\mathcal O_P(e)=\mathcal O_Y(e)$, this is ampleness of $r^*\mathcal O_P(e)$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, proof of (6) implies (1), using Properties Tags 01PU and 01Q2.

proof.text: The ring map and canonical morphism from Step 1 satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-trf-proj-canonical-map-twist-comparison] ($T$ is quasi-compact and the nonvanishing opens of positive-degree homogeneous elements cover $T$), so for some $d\geq1$ there is an isomorphism $r^*\mathcal O_P(dk)\simeq L|_T^{\otimes dk}$ for every $k\geq1$. Take $k=e$. With $e$ as in Step 3, [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample] (with $k=d$) says that the multiplication map $\mathcal O_Y(e)^{\otimes d}\to\mathcal O_Y(ed)$ is an isomorphism on $Y$; this identification is only asserted on the quasi-compact open $Y$, not on all of $P$ (for $A=k[x,y]$ with $\deg x=1$, $\deg y=2$, the map $\mathcal O_P(1)^{\otimes2}\to\mathcal O_P(2)$ is not surjective at the point of $D_+(y)$ where $x^2/y=0$). Since $r=u\circ i$ and pullback commutes with tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $r^*\mathcal O_P(ed)=i^*\mathcal O_Y(ed)\simeq(i^*\mathcal O_Y(e))^{\otimes d}$. This is ample by Step 3 and [lem-sc-ample-positive-tensor-power]. Hence $L|_T^{\otimes ed}\simeq r^*\mathcal O_P(ed)$ is ample.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, proof of (6) implies (1), paragraphs on the pullback of O(d) and ampleness of a quasi-compact open of Proj.

proof.text: Since $ed>0$, every affine nonvanishing section cover for the positive tensor power $L|_T^{\otimes ed}$ is also a cover by sections of positive tensor powers of $L|_T$ (with the same nonvanishing loci). Thus $L|_T$ is ample directly from [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. As this holds for the inverse image of every affine open $V\subseteq S$, the asserted relative ampleness follows from the quasi-compactness of $h$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, conclusion of (6) implies (1), together with Definition 01PS of ample and Definition 01VH of relatively ample.
